plants.name: Helianthus annuus
plants.description: Tall, sun-chasing stems carry broad golden-yellow petals around dark, seed-packed centers. Fields and prairie edges glow in mid-August, and bees crowd the blooms.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late summer, typically August through September in North America
plants.location: Prairies, fields and gardens across North America
plants.funFact: What looks like one flower is really a head of hundreds of tiny florets. The outer ones form the petals and the inner ones become seeds.

plants.name: Protea cynaroides
plants.description: The largest of all proteas, with a huge, artichoke-like bloom ringed by silky pink bracts. It is South Africa's national flower and stands out against the fynbos in the Southern Hemisphere winter.
plants.bloomingSeason: Winter to spring, mainly June to October
plants.location: Fynbos slopes of the Western and Eastern Cape, South Africa
plants.funFact: Proteas belong to an ancient plant family that is older than many continents' current positions. The thick-walled blooms are adapted to survive the periodic wildfires of the fynbos.

plants.name: Acacia pycnantha
plants.description: In late winter this Australian tree is covered in fluffy, fragrant golden pom-poms that light up bushland. It is Australia's national floral emblem.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late winter to spring, roughly July to October depending on region
plants.location: Southeastern Australia, including Victoria, South Australia and New South Wales
plants.funFact: The fluffy puffs are not petals. They are clusters of tiny flowers whose long yellow stamens make up most of the display.
